summary: The selected scenario is the 256-core Intel SCC-based 2-D chip (PACT vs HotSpot speed comparison, Table III/IV, PDF page 8). The 2D screening label is illustrative_2d_only, and the experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, which has no transient trace. Studio did NOT run: simulation status is skipped, simulation_allowed is false, and comparison_valid is false. The input gate failed because a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, and the extraction supplied an empty floorplan and no per-block powers. The scientific gate also failed and nothing is independently verified. The paper gives only a hot spot power density of 216.6 W/cm2 (2,166,000 W/m2), the Eris et al. (DATE 2018) power profile source, and speed results (max 1.9x steady-state and 232x transient speedup vs HotSpot). It reports no thermal observable with a page, unit, location, aggregation and regime, so there is no paper temperature to compare against and no Studio temperature was produced. No numerical comparison is made. Any qualitative statement is limited to this: the result would be sensitive to the package, heat sink, discretization and boundary assumptions, which were not specified for Studio. The pinned packet has no assets, so the source commit is unavailable. The linked PACT and OpenSTA repositories are not pinned and do not prove that the SCC inputs exist. No placement was generated, so no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace exists. The final verdict is gated off: this is not a replication and no exact match is claimed.

The paper gives no per-block floorplan (x, y, width, height) and no per-block watts for the 256-core SCC chip. Only a hot spot power density of 216.6 W/cm2 is stated, so no complete experiment can be reconstructed. The power profile comes from prior work (Eris et al.), which is not packaged.

The scenario reports simulation speed (Table IV). Its temperature results are not available in the extractable text, so no paper thermal observable value exists for comparison. The ~90 degC maximum and ~9 degC gradient quoted on page 11 belong to the separate OpenROAD MPSoC scenario.

The original solver is a compact RC netlist solved by Xyce on an MPI cluster, with a medium-cost heat spreader and heat sink, and the grid resolution is given only in Table III. A Studio solver, package and cooling model will differ in discretization and boundary conditions, so temperatures are not directly comparable.
The scenario has no optimizer and no controller, and the power trace is a single selected profile. The original does not exercise any optimizer or controller behavior to replicate.

The paper's monolithic 3-D, liquid-microchannel and 2.5-D PNoC cases are separate scenarios and are not used. The selected case is 2-D with a conventional heat sink, so no 3-D or interposer mismatch applies to the selected scenario.

No Studio package or material assumptions are supplied in the packet, so none can be recorded as paper-derived. Any Studio default stack, materials and heat sink would differ from the paper's medium-cost heat sink.
Any placement the runner generates would be illustrative and separate from paper facts, and its temperatures must not be numerically compared to the paper.
